title: codex-swap settings
description: Settings for codex-swap, stored as settings.json in the codex-swap data root. Every field is optional: anything absent falls back to the documented default, and unknown fields are preserved on round trip. A file that fails validation produces a stderr diagnostic and safe defaults rather than an error.

$schema.description: Reserved for editor tooling: path or URL of the JSON Schema describing this file. Ignored by codex-swap.

schemaVersion.description: Version of the settings file format.

selection.description: How an account is chosen when none is forced.

strategy.description: Default automatic selection strategy, overridable per invocation.

allowUnknown.description: Let accounts with unknown usage be selected automatically. They score as zero headroom, so any account with known headroom still wins. Equivalent to passing --allow-unknown on every invocation.

concurrencyPenaltyPercent.description: Headroom percentage points subtracted from an account's score for each of its active invocation leases, so work spreads across accounts instead of stacking on one.

defaultMaxConcurrent.description: Fallback cap on simultaneous invocation leases per account, applied only to accounts with no maxConcurrent policy of their own. null means no cap.

usage.description: Usage freshness, trust ceilings, and adaptive poll pacing.

serveTtlMs.description: A measurement younger than this is fresh: it is served without a network request and is decision-grade regardless of poll state.

normalTrustMaxAgeMs.description: Age ceiling past which a deliberately stale measurement stops being decision-grade after a network, timeout, parse, or server failure. Also caps a Retry-After honored on a non-429 response.

rateLimitTrustMaxAgeMs.description: Age ceiling that applies instead after a 429. Longer than the normal ceiling because usage only rises within a rate-limit window, so last-good stays a conservative lower bound.

fetchClaimTtlMs.description: How long one collector's claim to fetch an account's usage lasts, keeping concurrent processes from probing the same account at once.

minimumIntervalMs.description: Floor on the adaptive poll interval. Movement tightens pacing to this and no further.

activeDefaultIntervalMs.description: Starting poll interval for the active (most recently selected) account.

activeMaximumIntervalMs.description: Ceiling the active account's interval widens toward while its usage is calm.

candidateDefaultIntervalMs.description: Starting poll interval for candidate (non-active) accounts.

candidateMaximumIntervalMs.description: Ceiling a candidate account's interval widens toward while its usage is calm.

exhaustedIntervalMs.description: Floor on the poll interval for an account at or past its limit, holding exhausted accounts to a slow cadence.

urgentIntervalMs.description: Poll interval for an active account whose binding window is past the near-exhaustion threshold and still rising. Suppressed while a 429 is recent.

movementDeltaPercent.description: Change in the binding window's used percentage that counts as movement. Movement halves the interval; calm widens it by half again toward the role ceiling.

jitterFraction.description: Random spread applied to poll intervals and failure backoff, plus or minus this fraction, keeping processes and machines out of lockstep.

post429MinimumIntervalMs.description: Floor on the poll interval while a 429 is recent.

post429MaximumIntervalMs.description: Ceiling on the poll interval while a 429 is recent.

recent429WindowMs.description: How long after a 429 an account counts as recently rate-limited, applying post-429 pacing and suppressing urgent mode.

resetSlackMs.description: Grace period added after a known future window reset before polling for the refreshed quota. A reset can only pull the next poll earlier, never later.

retryAfterCapMs.description: Upper bound on a Retry-After honored from a 429, so a malformed value cannot park an account indefinitely.

probeFallback.description: What to do when the direct usage endpoint is unavailable. 'disabled' returns a clear capability error; 'header-probe' falls back to a real inference request read for quota headers, which consumes quota.

reservationTtlMs.description: How long a reserved invocation lease stays valid before its child process is marked running.

heartbeatIntervalMs.description: How often a running invocation heartbeats its lease.

runningExpiryMs.description: How long a running lease stays valid after its last heartbeat before another process may treat it as expired.

attachTui.description: Launch run/resume against the leased account's resident app-server with --remote when one is registered. The server is pinned to the same account, so billing is unchanged; attaching puts the session where app-server clients can see it. Disable to always launch a standalone Codex.

dedicated.description: Give every run/resume its own exclusive app-server by default — pinned to the leased account, torn down with the session — so a session's socket is its identity. Equivalent to passing --server auto on every launch; --server/--no-server override per launch. Falls back to a plain launch, saying so on stderr, only when no dedicated server can run at all.
